line: Hi. Sol. If you hear someone muttering drug names, that's me. Nursing school. Pharmacology is trying to kill me.
Beta blockers. Everything ends in '-olol.' I've been my family's interpreter since I was eight, so I figured I might as well get paid for the medical part.
choice3: I'll let you get back to it.

line: My mom's doctor visits. 'Tell him it hurts here, but not like before.' Try that at eight. Now I make my little cousins do it. Either progress or a cycle.
They mind everything, they're nine. I coach their soccer team Saturdays. Half the parents yell in Spanish, half in English. The kids ignore both equally.
Exam Friday. My mom lit a candle for me at San José and also told me to get some sleep. She knows those are opposite instructions.
My mom volunteers me for the pantry. I hand out bags and translate the rules sheet for Mr. Funes, who reads it more carefully than anyone alive.
choice2: Your mom drives a hard bargain.

line: Weird question. At school I'm the Mexican one. At my tía's I'm the gringa who says 'like' too much. Do you ever feel like the visiting team everywhere?
choice2: Not really. I'm home team both places.

line: My dad's had a green card thirty years. He made us all practise what to say if someone stops the car. My little brother laughed. My dad didn't.
The clinic is hiring paid interpreters now. My clinical instructor asked if I'd thought about it. I've been doing it for free for sixteen years.
You're at the hall every time I'm dragged here. Pilar's going to put you on the fiesta committee. She did it to me in 2019. I'm still on it.
Saw you at the library trivia night. You missed the one about the Rio Grande. I said nothing. I'm a good person.
Can't, I'm on flashcard forty of two hundred. If I stop now I'll forget the first thirty-nine.
